notes:
Key account for Q3; heavy focus on throughput guarantees for trading inference.
- Primary ask: dedicated GPU pool with firm min tokens/sec guarantee and explicit concurrency caps per model.
- Trading use-case: market signal scoring + short text reranking; tail latency risk unacceptable during open market hours.
- Preliminary numbers discussed on call: target sustained aggregate >= 12,000 tokens/sec for llm-13b-v2 (quantized), per-request concurrency cap 16, per-session token limits.
- Burst policy: customer wants 1.5x sustained for up to 2 minutes with cooldown/backoff, and automatic fallback to smaller model variant if sustained > 3x for >5 minutes.
- POC plan: Redwood to provision a dedicated 4xA100-equivalent pool (reserved) for 2 weeks; run synthetic and replay tests with 2M token trace from Jan-Feb.
- Acceptance criteria: 95th pct latency < 120ms for generation windows <= 128 tokens at 12k tokens/sec aggregate; no >1% error rate on token outputs; cost per token within agreed ARR band.
- Security: require SSO + SAML, KMS integration for key wrapping, audit logs to be retained 12 months, and regionally-resident cache in us-west-2.
- Legal: counterproposal pending — wants SLA credit thresholds lowered for P95/P99 breaches; our standard requires negotiation on sustained breach windows and force majeure carveouts.
- Quote: customer prefers monthly reserved commit with burst buckets vs flat overprovisioning. They asked for model routing policy: route to cheaper quantized variant outside market hours.
- Quote from CTO: "We need predictable throughput during market open — even a short stall costs real dollars."
- Notes from SE: must validate KV cache eviction behavior under concurrent sessions; KV warmup strategy needs to be part of SOW.
- Internal: sales to propose two procurement options: (A) higher commit, smaller burst, tighter credits; (B) lower commit, larger burst pool at premium.
- Next milestone: finalize min tokens/sec and formal burst SLA by 2026-03-15, then legal review week of 2026-03-22.
